subject: business_studies

concepts.title: Private Sector and Public Sector in a Mixed Economy
concepts.definition: A framework where economic operations are divided between privately owned entities seeking profit and government-owned entities serving public interest.
concepts.key_idea: Coexistence of privately owned firms and state-managed organizations within the economy.
question_patterns: explain the difference between private sector and public sector enterprises
what is a mixed economy in the context of business ownership
differentiate private and public sector based on ownership and control
identify the two main sectors operating in the Indian economy
Explain private sector and public sector in a mixed economy in your own words.

solution_steps.explain: Determine whether the enterprise is owned by private individuals or state entities.
Check if primary goal is profit earning (private) or social welfare and public accountability (public).

concepts.title: Departmental Undertakings
concepts.definition: Public sector units established as direct departments of a ministry without an independent legal identity, financed directly through government budgetary allocations.
concepts.key_idea: Direct ministry control without separate legal entity status.
question_patterns: explain the features of departmental undertakings
what are the merits and limitations of departmental undertakings
why are railways and post offices organized as departmental undertakings
how are departmental undertakings financed and controlled
Explain departmental undertakings in your own words.

solution_steps.explain: Verify that the unit functions as an extension of a ministry and lacks a separate corporate entity.
Confirm funding originates from the government treasury via annual appropriations and revenue is deposited back into the treasury.

concepts.title: Statutory Corporations
concepts.definition: Autonomous corporate bodies created by a special parliamentary act specifying their powers, functions, employee service rules, and financial independence.
concepts.key_idea: Parliamentary act creation combining government authority with operational autonomy.
question_patterns: what is a statutory corporation and its features
how does a statutory corporation differ from a departmental undertaking
explain the merits and limitations of statutory corporations
why are statutory corporations given financial autonomy
Explain statutory corporations in your own words.

solution_steps.explain: Confirm the organization was established by a Special Act of Parliament or state legislature.

solution_steps.action: verify legal personality and financial autonomy
solution_steps.explain: Verify that the corporation is a body corporate capable of suing, entering contracts, acquiring property, and managing its own finances.

concepts.title: Government Company Shareholding Criteria
concepts.definition: A company formed under the Companies Act where a minimum of 51 percent of total paid-up share capital is held by the central government, state governments, or a combination thereof.
concepts.key_idea: A minimum of 51% paid-up capital held by government grants government company status.
question_patterns: calculate the government shareholding percentage to determine government company status
find the minimum government capital required for a company to become a government company
what percentage of paid-up capital must government hold in a government company
compute whether a given equity distribution satisfies government company criteria
Explain government company shareholding criteria in your own words.

solution_steps.explain: Divide government-owned capital by total paid-up share capital and multiply by 100.

solution_steps.action: calculate minimum required capital for 51 percent ownership threshold
solution_steps.explain: Compute 51 percent of total paid-up capital to verify the minimum state contribution needed.

worked_examples.question: Solve a typical question involving government company shareholding criteria.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: calculate government share percentage. Step 2: calculate minimum required capital for 51 percent ownership threshold. Working: (govt_capital / total_capital) * 100, (total_capital * 51) / 100.
worked_examples.answer: Government Company Shareholding Criteria applied step by step gives the required result.

worked_examples.question: Apply government company shareholding criteria to a fresh example and interpret the result.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: calculate government share percentage. Step 2: calculate minimum required capital for 51 percent ownership threshold. Working: (govt_capital / total_capital) * 100, (total_capital * 51) / 100.
worked_examples.answer: The method of government company shareholding criteria leads to the required value or conclusion.

concepts.title: Changing Role of Public Sector and Industrial Policy Reforms
concepts.definition: Refers to the policy shifts post-1991 redefining public sector priorities from monopolies and heavy capital investment toward competitiveness, disinvestment, and reduced sector reservations.
concepts.key_idea: Reorienting state enterprises through disinvestment, BIFR referrals, MoUs, and reduced reserved areas.
question_patterns: describe the government policy towards the public sector since 1991
what is disinvestment of shares in public sector enterprises
how has the number of reserved industries for public sector changed over time
explain the role of Memorandum of Understanding in public enterprises
Explain changing role of public sector and industrial policy reforms in your own words.

solution_steps.explain: Identify major policy elements: strategic equity reduction, disinvestment, MoU accountability, and BIFR referral for sick units.
Trace reduction of reserved industries from 17 (in 1956) down to 8 (in 1991) and eventually 3 core areas.

concepts.title: Global Enterprises (Multinational Corporations)
concepts.definition: Gigantic industrial concerns that extend production, commercial, and marketing operations across multiple countries from a centralized home country headquarters.
concepts.key_idea: Transnational operations characterized by vast financial resources, advanced technology, and centralized management.
question_patterns: what are global enterprises and state their main features
why do multinational corporations dominate international markets
explain how foreign collaboration and product innovation help global enterprises
how does centralized control work in multinational corporations
Explain global enterprises (multinational corporations) in your own words.

solution_steps.explain: Check if the enterprise operates network branches and subsidiaries across multiple host nations.
Assess attributes such as massive capital, advanced technology, aggressive marketing, and parent headquarters control.

concepts.title: Joint Ventures
concepts.definition: A business partnership formed when two or more independent organizations pool assets, technical expertise, and risks to achieve shared commercial objectives.
concepts.key_idea: Mutual resource pooling between distinct businesses, categorized as contractual or equity-based.
question_patterns: what is a joint venture and explain its benefits
differentiate between contractual joint venture and equity-based joint venture
why do foreign firms form joint ventures with domestic companies
explain how joint ventures provide access to new markets and technology
Explain joint ventures in your own words.

solution_steps.explain: Determine whether the agreement creates a new corporate entity (equity-based) or relies on a contractual cooperation scheme (contractual).
Identify gained synergies such as low production cost, established brand equity, advanced technology, or market entry.

concepts.title: Public Private Partnership (PPP)
concepts.definition: A long-term collaborative framework between government bodies and private enterprises for designing, financing, building, and operating public infrastructure projects.
concepts.key_idea: Optimal risk distribution and efficiency sharing between government and private entities for public projects.
question_patterns: explain the concept and main features of public private partnership
what are the strengths and weaknesses of the PPP model
give examples of sectors where public private partnerships are commonly used
how are tasks and risks allocated in a public private partnership
Explain public private partnership (ppp) in your own words.

solution_steps.explain: Verify collaboration between state agency (ministry/municipality) and private investor/operator.

solution_steps.action: assess risk allocation and role distribution
solution_steps.explain: Check that design, construction, or operational risks are transferred to private partner while public authority ensures social obligations.

Calculate the percentage of share capital held by the government and find the minimum government contribution required for majority control as a government company.

extracted_variables.total_capital: total paid-up capital of the enterprise in INR
extracted_variables.govt_capital: share capital owned by government in INR

solution_template.explain: Divide government-owned capital by total paid-up share capital and multiply by 100.

solution_template.action: calculate minimum required capital for 51 percent ownership threshold
solution_template.explain: Compute 51 percent of total paid-up capital to verify the minimum state contribution needed.
